msx88va - an MSX1 cartridge player for the NEC PC-88VA and PC-88VA2

This disk is MS-DOS 4.0 for the PC-88VA (FreeDOS-88VA project, MIT
licence) with MSX.COM. AUTOEXEC.BAT runs MSX.

  MSX [/N] [cartridge.ROM]
  MSX /R

MSX.COM needs, in the current directory:

  CBIOS_M1.ROM, CBIOS_L1.ROM  C-BIOS 0.29a, an open-source MSX BIOS
                              (two-clause BSD licence, see CBIOS.TXT)

An MSX1 main ROM of your own (32 KiB) named MSXBIOS.ROM is used instead
of C-BIOS when it is in the current directory; none is included.

MSX.COM plays a cartridge ROM file: 8, 16 or 32 KiB, without a mapper. Copy
your own ROM files to this disk (under MS-DOS, or with add_files.py on a
disk image). Without an argument MSX runs the one *.ROM file of the
current directory other than C-BIOS, shows a menu when there are several,
and starts C-BIOS alone when there is none. No cartridge ROM is included.

Free games: on a PC with Python 3,

  python3 get_games.py msx88va.d88

downloads eight freeware MSX1 games of the MSXdev contest from
msxdev.org and writes msx88va-games.d88 with them and GAMES.TXT (their
authors and pages). The games belong to their authors.

Keys: the VA keyboard is the MSX keyboard. Joystick 1: cursor keys,
SPACE or Z (trigger A), X (trigger B). HELP resets the MSX. To leave,
switch the machine off or reset it.

Display: 256x192 inside a 320x200 screen. Sound: the PSG on the OPN's SSG.

Graphics I (most 1984 games) is drawn with the VA's user-defined
characters (gaiji), which is faster. They live in battery-backed RAM, so
MSX first saves them to GAIJI.BAK on this disk (the disk must be
writable; an existing GAIJI.BAK is kept). To put your own characters
back, press . (or ESC) in the cartridge menu to return to DOS and run

  MSX /R

which restores them from GAIJI.BAK and deletes it. MSX /N leaves the
characters alone and draws everything in graphics memory.

msx88va: two-clause BSD licence (LICENSE.TXT).
